tweets.text:
The reason India has terrible roads that break down during monsoon rains is explained phenomenally in this hidden blog by legendary civil engineer PS Kandhal.

The MoRTH/IRC highway specs includes 7 water-trapping bitumen mixes which don't last >1-2yrs. Construction contractors make way more on higher life cycle costs, recurring annual tenders with "fat" pothole repair budgets.

There are also tons of other reasons like a) cutting roads for utility lines without a rebuild b) poor auditing c) straight up using worse materials than the spec d) over-use of funds to visible public roads that causes budget issues, and e) contractors bribing the govt to secure contracts.

If it's not abundantly obvious, what makes it disgusting is because it games a system clearly not designed to be treated this way and makes it unfair to others within the same company who just do consistent good work that may not lead to a crescendo during a promo cycle.

It's totally fine that people respond to their incentive structure but this is deliberate reward hacking which I find to be in poor taste. Fine if you disagree with that.
